title: Pac-Man
shortDescription: Toru Iwatani's pop-culture phenomenon that defined early arcade gaming and introduced character-driven gameplay.
historicalSignificance: Created the maze-action genre, pioneered character branding in video games, and became an enduring worldwide cultural icon.

editorialContent.overview: First tested at the Shibuya Cinema building in Tokyo on May 22, 1980, Pac-Man was conceived by young Namco designer Toru Iwatani as a deliberate counter-programming alternative to the violent space shooters dominating Japanese amusement centers. Guided by the Japanese onomatopoeia 'paku paku' (munching) and shaped like a pizza with a slice removed, the yellow character captured global fascination, generating hundreds of millions in coin-op revenue and establishing video games as mainstream pop culture.
editorialContent.gameplayMechanics: Unlike contemporary titles relying on twitch shooting, Pac-Man is an exercise in route optimization and enemy prediction. The labyrinth features 244 standard dots and four large Energizer power pellets that invert hunter and hunted. What elevated the game mathematically was the distinct algorithmic personality programmed into each ghost: Blinky (Shadow) relentlessly tracks Pac-Man's exact coordinates; Pinky (Speedy) targets positions four tiles ahead of Pac-Man's trajectory; Inky (Bashful) calculates vectors based on both Blinky and Pac-Man; and Clyde (Pokey) alternates between pursuing Pac-Man and retreating to the bottom-left corner based on distance thresholds.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Engineered for Namco's proprietary arcade hardware, Pac-Man operated on an 8-bit Zilog Z80 processor running at 3.072 MHz accompanied by a custom Namco 3-channel wave-table sound generator. Displayed on a vertically mounted 3:4 CRT monitor at 224 × 288 resolution with 16 simultaneous colors from a 32-color palette, the codebase occupies just 16 kilobytes of ROM. The famous 'Split-Screen' bug at Level 256 occurs due to an 8-bit integer overflow where the fruit-drawing routine attempts to draw 256 fruit icons, corrupting the right half of the screen buffer into hexadecimal memory garbage.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Pac-Man was the first video game to transcend the medium into a global marketing empire. It spawned over 400 licensed commercial products—from lunchboxes and apparel to a Saturday morning Hanna-Barbera cartoon and Buckner & Garcia's Billboard Top 10 single 'Pac-Man Fever' in 1982. Crucially, its whimsical theme and non-violent premise welcomed women and casual players into video arcades for the first time in industry history.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved across multiple ROM revisions (Midway US upright/cocktail and Namco original Japanese sets). Historical preservation requires careful attention to the 60Hz vertical refresh rate (60.606061 Hz) and authentic CRT beam curvature for scanline accuracy.
